authority: control 0.0.1 over stdio is the only authority; the CDP edge translates each qualified method into a native operation executed by the host's main loop against the same targets, frames and revisions; the edge holds target names and adapter-scoped ids only, never a target, realm or profile

transport.listen: 127.0.0.1 only; --cdp-port PORT (0 = ephemeral) with --ready-file PATH; non-loopback peers are dropped
transport.websocket: GET /devtools/browser/native-dom-control; RFC 6455 accept; client frames must be masked; no fragmentation; text, ping and close opcodes only

bounds.connections: one at a time, served sequentially

adapter.registration: Target.attachToTarget registers an adapter record {kind: cdp, target} in the host; owners.adapters counts them; target.close and session.close detach every adapter of the closed target and report adapters_detached
adapter.handle: a CDP session holds the native target id and an adapter id; every command re-resolves the target through the host, so a closed target answers -32000 'target closed; adapter detached' and the session is dropped
adapter.frame_ids: Page.FrameId is adapter-scoped per connection (cdp_frame_N), one-to-one with a native frame id while both live, never equal to the native id, kept across same-frame navigation because the native frame id is kept
adapter.execution_contexts: Runtime.ExecutionContextId is never emitted; realms are not projected

qualified.Browser.getVersion: product and protocol strings; no browser identity beyond this host
qualified.Target.setDiscoverTargets: discover=true replays live native targets as Target.targetCreated events after the response
qualified.Target.setAutoAttach: browser-level autoAttach=true replays live native targets as flattened Target.attachedToTarget sessions announced before the response (waitingForDebugger=false), each an adapter record; session-level calls are acknowledged only
qualified.Target.getTargets: live native targets as type page
qualified.Target.attachToTarget: flatten=true required; registers an adapter; -32000 when the target does not exist
qualified.Target.detachFromTarget: drops the session and its adapter record
qualified.Page.getFrameTree: the native target.inspect frames[] projected through adapter-scoped ids; the native host has one main frame, so childFrames is empty
qualified.DOM.getDocument: root document node; childNodeCount is the semantic node count; refreshes the session's node table
qualified.DOM.querySelector: document-rooted only; selectors button, a and #id; returns a session-scoped nodeId
qualified.DOM.resolveNode: session-scoped objectId over the node reference (target, revision, node)
qualified.Runtime.callFunctionOn: functionDeclaration function(){this.click();} only; a click on a link is the native same-frame navigation; a revision mismatch is -32000

methods.why: acknowledging Page.enable, Runtime.enable or Network.enable without their events would emulate support; the native host has no execution-context, lifecycle or network events to project

claimed: browser.targets() / waitForTarget lists exactly the native target ids
session.send for every qualified method above
not_claimed: target.page() and any Page API of puppeteer: its initialization needs Network.enable, Page.enable, Runtime.enable and lifecycle events, all explicit -32601 here
Playwright, Chromium, Electron or any other client or engine

court.script: labs/native-dom/cdp-frame-tree-court.py drives stdio itself (requests validated by protocol/check_contract.py) and drives puppeteer-core through labs/native-dom/puppeteer-frame-tree.mjs over a command channel
steps: stdio opens target A (semantic-nav.html) and target B (semantic-static.html)
puppeteer connects, discovers exactly {A, B}, attaches a session to A
Page.getFrameTree on A: one frame, no children, adapter-scoped id that differs from the native frame id; the court records the mapping
puppeteer clicks the in-court link on A through DOM.querySelector('a') / DOM.resolveNode / Runtime.callFunctionOn
stdio verifies on A: revision +1, generation 2, new realm, retired realm not_found, old node reference stale_revision
puppeteer re-fetches the document, sees the new node count, Page.getFrameTree keeps the same frame id; it clicks the new document's button and stdio sees revision +1 again
puppeteer's session on A cannot see B: Page.getFrameTree on a session attached to B yields different ids; a session id from another connection is unknown
stdio closes A: the puppeteer session's next command is -32000 'target closed; adapter detached'; owners.adapters drops by one
puppeteer detaches from B and disconnects; owners.adapters is zero; stdio closes B and the session
memory owners and footprint are sampled at empty, live (A and B open with sessions attached), and post-close, under the default allocator and the opt-in arena
court.pass_rule: every step is a typed check; any failure is recorded and the receipt's passed flag is false; no host or server restart is used to recover

unchanged: no Web API, child frame or Runtime realm projection
the network policy and budgets are those of target.open and link navigation

revisions_after_freeze.what: Target.targetCreated (after setDiscoverTargets) and Target.attachedToTarget (after setAutoAttach and attachToTarget) are written before the command's response; Target.detachedFromTarget after detachFromTarget
revisions_after_freeze.why: puppeteer-core builds its target list and its CDPSession objects from events received during the command; events after the response left browser.targets() empty and createCDPSession failing
revisions_after_freeze.effect: none on the qualified method set; the frozen text said 'after the response' for targetCreated

revisions_after_freeze.what: adapter counts equal the sessions the client holds: the auto-attach replay registers one adapter per live target and every createCDPSession adds one more
revisions_after_freeze.why: an auto-attached target is what puppeteer-core exposes as available; the court therefore expects 2 adapters after connect with two targets, 3 after createCDPSession on A, 4 with both explicit sessions, 2 after A closes over stdio, 1 after the explicit B session detaches, 0 after disconnect
revisions_after_freeze.effect: court expectations state these counts explicitly; a first draft that acknowledged setAutoAttach without replay was withdrawn because it left the client without any available target
